svg.text: Sample evidence → decision under H₀. A test does not turn uncertainty into certainty.

text.tspan: H₀: baseline / no effect (e.g., fair coin). [S1–S3]
A sample-based number from the sample. [S2]
Rejection region: values that reject H₀;
acceptance region: values that do not. [S2]
How the statistic behaves assuming H₀
is true; it sets the comparison baseline.
Used to judge how extreme the result is. [S2]
Probability under H₀ of a result as or
more extreme than the observed result. [S3]
Choose the rejection cutoff before testing;
p ≤ α → reject H₀; p > α → fail to reject H₀.
Do not claim certainty from one sample. [S1–S3]

svg.text: Set the cutoff before examining the test result.
Use the sample to compute a test statistic.
Use the null distribution to obtain a p-value.
Compare p with α; explain business impact.
Chance of 3 or fewer heads if the coin is fair.
Interpretation: the result is not unusual enough
at this cutoff to reject the fair-coin baseline.
⚠ Source inconsistency: one later line says “cutoff 0.5”.
This example otherwise specifies α = 0.05; use that value here.
Reject H₀ even though it is true. [S1]
Fail to reject H₀ even though it is false. [S1]
Probability the test rejects H₀ when H₀ is false. [S1]
Easier rejection → more power, but more Type I errors; stricter cutoff →
fewer rejections and potentially lower power. [S1–S3]
the 17.1% p-value is for the lower-tail setup. [S3]
Wording varies: “accept H₀” vs “fail to reject H₀”; CI link not developed. [S1–S3].

text.tspan: p > α: fail to reject H₀
